title: Higher-order interactions for controlling time-delayed Kuramoto model
authors: Narumi Fujii, Martin Moriamé, Maxime Lucas, Hiroya Nakao, Timoteo Carletti
abstract: We propose a framework for controlling the collective dynamics of the time-delayed Kuramoto model based on a delay-free, higher-order approximation of the delayed interactions. By applying the Ott--Antonsen ansatz and the second-order averaging method to the resulting higher-order Kuramoto model, we obtain a one-dimensional reduced equation for the order parameter dynamics. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the higher-order approximation predicts the dynamics of the original delayed system more accurately than the conventional pairwise approximation and enables the realization of bistability and intermediate synchronization states. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of higher-order interpretations of time delays for the control of oscillator networks with time-delayed interactions.
summary: This paper tackles controlling synchronization in a time-delayed Kuramoto model by replacing the delay with an equivalent, higher-order interaction term. Using advanced mathematical techniques like the Ott–Antonsen ansatz and second-order averaging, they derive a simplified ODE that accurately predicts complex behaviors like bistability, outperforming simpler approximations.
main_problem: To develop a delay-free control framework for managing the collective synchronization dynamics of the time-delayed Kuramoto model.
main_result: The higher-order approximation accurately predicts system dynamics, enabling the realization and tuning of bistability and intermediate synchronization states via mean-field feedback control.
method: The authors use perturbation theory combined with the Ott–Antonsen ansatz and second-order averaging methods to reduce the infinite-dimensional delay differential equation into a manageable one-dimensional ODE for the order parameter.
model_or_system: The system is the globally coupled time-delayed Kuramoto model, which describes $N$ phase oscillators interacting with time delays. The analysis focuses on deriving an effective, higher-order approximation of these delayed interactions.
key_observables: Order parameter $z(t) = R(t)e^{i\Psi(t)}$, where $R$ is the degree of synchronization and $\Psi$ is the collective phase.
important_parameters: The small coupling strength ($\epsilon$) and the time delay ($	au$) are crucial parameters, with accuracy depending on the product $\epsilon	au$.
main_assumptions: The primary assumptions involve deriving a higher-order approximation valid for small $\epsilon	au$, and applying the second-order averaging method to achieve $O(\epsilon^2)$ accuracy.
figures_summary: Figures compare stability diagrams and prediction errors between the higher-order approximation, the simpler pairwise approximation, and direct numerical simulations across different control inputs and delay strengths.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first deriving the higher-order, delay-free approximation of the delayed Kuramoto model. It then applies the Ott–Antonsen ansatz and uses second-order averaging to obtain a reduced ODE for $R$. Finally, it analyzes this equation under various mean-field control inputs, comparing results against simpler approximations.
why_interesting: While focused on classical oscillators, the mathematical techniques—such as deriving effective dynamics from complex time-delayed systems using systematic approximation methods (like averaging)—are highly relevant to modeling open quantum systems or many-body dynamics where memory effects or non-Markovian noise are present.
